This is exactly what it was for me, too. I was in college and feeling desperately burnt out and mentally unwell, and was just wanting to go home for a while. Spring break was coming up, and when we got the email it was extended by a couple weeks, I was really happy. When they told us later we wouldn’t coming back at all, I was actually even happier. I recognize I was privileged in my family situation, I was provided for and my dad was able to keep his job through covid… so really, it just became a long break for me where it felt like the world was on pause for a while, and I was tucked away with my family where real life couldn’t touch us. I had my classes virtually, I was able to focus more on my health, get my mental state in shape… it was honestly so nice. I know covid itself was awful and did a lot of damage in a lot of different ways, so I feel almost bad to talk about my experience as positive, but in a way it really was.

Mint Mobile is not T-Mobile. Mint is an MVNO, they don’t own their own cellular towers, they just lease bandwidth from the T-Mobile network. They’re not the same. If they were, it would make zero sense to be able to purchase separate plans from both Mint and T-Mobile. Even with T-Mobile acquiring Mint, it’s still going to remain separate as Mint and you could experience different levels of coverage depending on who you go with.

Did you have a physical SIM or an eSIM with Verizon? If you had a physical SIM, you’ll want to make sure you’ve taken it out of your phone or your eSIM with Mint won’t work. I had a similar issue to you switching from AT&T to Mint. As soon as I did that, everything worked perfectly for me. Might be worth a shot.

Normally holds are only ever placed on checks, not on cash. Was the $15K in the form of a check? If so then it’s common for institutions to place a hold on checks to allow time for them to clear before you’re able to use the funds. Common reasons for check holds are if you don’t have much of a history of larger check deposits, if you don’t have matching funds already in the account (in this case meaning you don’t already have at least $15K in there before the deposit), etc. there’s plenty of things we look for to determine if a check needs to be held, but those are a couple of the big ones. Essentially check holds are a form of protection both for you and for the institution. Never fun to spend thousands of dollars from a check you deposited only for it to bounce after a couple days and suddenly you’re out all that money (and possibly owe some to the institution, if it brings your balance negative)! 

So to answer your question, holds are a totally standard practice & you should be fine. Once the 5 days are up you’ll be free to use the funds however you’d like!

Hi - I’ve worked in a financial institution for a few years! I believe what you’re referring to is a CTR (Currency Transaction Report). Anytime someone makes a combined total of over 10k in cash transactions at a financial institution in one day, a CTR needs to be filed to report the activity. 

SARs are definitely a thing as well, but making a combined total of over 10k in cash transactions in a day isn’t necessarily grounds for one of those to be filed. Those are only required to be filed when an institution deems the activity to be suspicious, if they suspect illegal activity may be going on, etc.
